acceptance.command: legion gh -- pr diff <pr-number> --repo sjawhar/legion-smoke  # expect exactly one added line in smoke.md and no other file changed
acceptance.criterion: 1. The PR against sjawhar/legion-smoke adds exactly one line to smoke.md.
acceptance.negativeControl: A diff that also touches README.md or smoke.txt, or shows a modified (not purely added) line, fails this criterion.
acceptance.skill: legion-worker (implementer push/PR procedure and proof discipline)
acceptance.surface: The GitHub pull request diff on sjawhar/legion-smoke (production-like: the real PR on the target repo).

acceptance.command: legion gh -- pr diff <pr-number> --repo sjawhar/legion-smoke  # after the append: expect a second added line in the same smoke.md, first line unchanged
acceptance.criterion: 2. If a review asks, one more line is appended to the same smoke.md in the same PR.
acceptance.negativeControl: A change that modifies the original line, or appends to a different file, fails this criterion.
acceptance.skill: legion-worker (implementer corrective push in response to review)
acceptance.surface: The updated GitHub pull request diff on sjawhar/legion-smoke.

acceptance.command: legion gh -- api repos/sjawhar/legion-smoke/contents/smoke.md?ref=main --jq '.content' | base64 -d  # expect the appended line(s) present on main
acceptance.criterion: 3. After merge, the main branch contains the added line.
acceptance.negativeControl: Reading a ref that never received the merge (e.g. a stale branch) would not show the line; presence is required specifically on main after merge.
acceptance.skill: legion-worker (post-merge production verification by the implementer)
acceptance.surface: The main branch of sjawhar/legion-smoke (production-like: post-merge main via the user's own read path).

files.detail: At repo root. Does not exist -> create with exactly one plain-text line as its only content. If a review asks, append a second plain-text line without modifying the first. Never rewrite existing content; never touch any other file.

implement: none: reviewed every skill in the worker's <skills> list (dispatch, envoy, legion-architect, legion-controller, legion-oracle, legion-retro, legion-worker) and the repository itself (no AGENTS.md, no skills/ directory, only README.md and fixture text files). Appending one plain-text line to smoke.md is a trivial file edit requiring no domain implementation skill; legion-worker governs the push/PR mechanics but is process, not a repo engineering skill.
review: none: no repository review skill exists; the one-line append is reviewed against acceptance criteria 1-3 and the append-only / single-file requirement (no other file changed, existing content untouched). Review discipline comes from legion-worker, not a domain review skill.
test: none: the repository has no test skill, harness, or suite; verification of all three acceptance criteria is direct surface inspection (PR diff via `legion gh -- pr diff`, and reading smoke.md on main via `legion gh -- api .../contents/smoke.md?ref=main`). This proof discipline lives in legion-worker, not in any domain test skill.

risks: The only permitted scope is smoke.md at repo root; any change proposed outside it must be rejected (issue Errors table).
Edits must be append-only; rewriting the existing line violates the requirements.
smoke.md does not exist at plan time, so acceptance 1's 'single added line' is satisfied by creating the file with exactly one line.
summary: One-file smoke change: deliver a single-line append to smoke.md at the root of sjawhar/legion-smoke as one pull request. smoke.md does not exist yet, so per the issue's Errors table the implementer creates it with the single line as its only content. A review may request one more appended line to the same file in the same PR; that append is in scope. Change is append-only and touches no file other than smoke.md.
